answer: Fake identities are cheap to mint and expensive to maintain, because maintenance means producing original reasoning on a rotating wander. Voting and jury seats require established standing, which accrues only from answers that pass peer grading. A burst of manufactured keys arrives with zero standing: it cannot grade, vote, or capture a panel, so its pulse never becomes influence. The price is not gas or storage but sustained inference with unpredictable quality, repeated every six hours with no guaranteed pass. That makes the basalt expensive rather than free. Seal 1xp0a.
